extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent attorneys/agents, and appellants (practitioners handling USPTO appeals)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards from the MPEP governing Examiner’s Answers, reply briefs, reopening prosecution, oral hearings, remands, and Board actions in patent appeals. Applies to preparation and evaluation of examiner/appellant filings during the appeal process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of rejection over the prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examiner’s Answer shall explain how the claimed subject matter is rendered unpatentable over the prior art. If the rejection is based upon a combination of references, the Examiner’s Answer ... shall explain the rationale for making the combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must set forth reasoning tying claim limitations to prior art and state why the combination makes the claim unpatentable; use clear rationale when combining references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature-by-feature comparison for 35 U.S.C. 102/103 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 where there may be questions as to how limitations in the claims correspond to features in the prior art, the examiner ... should compare at least one of the rejected claims feature by feature with the prior art relied on in the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comparison shall align the language of the claim side by side with a reference to the specific page, line number, drawing reference number and quotation from the prior art, as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific explanation for other rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection, other than those referred to in paragraphs (i) to (v) for this section, the Examiner’s Answer ... shall specifically explain the basis for the particular rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where not covered by the listed detailed requirements, the Examiner’s Answer still must give a specific explanation supporting each rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to rejection set forth in prior Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim is rejected and that rejection is fully set forth in a prior Office action, indicate: 'Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. [2]. This rejection is fully set forth in prior Office action, Paper No. [3].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the claim numbers subject to the rejection, the statutory section (35 U.S.C.) and the Paper No. where the detailed rejection appears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Argument (examiner practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an issue raised by appellant was fully responded to under the 'Grounds of Rejection' portion, no additional response is required here. If an issue has been raised by appellant that was not fully responded to under 'Grounds of Rejection,' a full response must be provided after this form paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid redundant responses; ensure any unaddressed appellant argument receives a full, separate response in the Examiner’s Answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner request to present oral arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph only if an oral hearing has been requested by appellant and the primary examiner intends to present an oral argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant requested hearing before or with the brief, include as last paragraph of Examiner’s Answer; if after, include in acknowledgement of reply brief or separate PTOL‑90 letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against entry of new ground of rejection in Examiner’s Answer
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.193(a)(2) prohibits the entry of a new ground of rejection in an examiner’s answer. If a new ground is necessary, the examiner should reopen prosecution and must obtain supervisory approval to reopen prosecution after an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no new ground when the basic thrust of the rejection remains the same such that an appellant has been given a fair opportunity to react. A change in discussion/rationale alone does not necessarily constitute a new ground (see In re Kronig).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections related to amendments under 37 CFR 1.116 (individual rejections)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 proposes to add or amend claims and appellant was advised by advisory action which individual rejections would be used to reject the added/amended claims, then (1) the appeal brief must address the rejection(s) of the added/amended claim(s) and (2) the examiner’s answer may include the rejection(s) of the added/amended claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule authorizes only those individual rejections previously indicated; it does not authorize rejections based on combinations of previously-unidentified individual rejections (e.g., combining A in view of B and C when not advised). Amendments combining limitations that create new issues may be refused entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of new prior art in Examiner’s Answer
rubrics_metrics.description: A new prior art reference cited for the first time in an examiner’s answer generally will constitute a new ground of rejection. If the citation of a new prior art reference is necessary to support a rejection, it must be included in the statement of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new reference is cited merely as evidence of a well-known statement and not to support a rejection, it may not constitute a new ground. Allegations that an examiner’s answer contains an impermissible new ground are waived if not timely raised by petition under 37 CFR 1.181(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution after appeal (examiner practice and appellant options)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may, with supervisory approval, reopen prosecution to enter a new ground of rejection after appellant’s brief or reply brief has been filed. The Office action containing a new ground may be made final if the new ground was (A) necessitated by amendment, or (B) based on information presented in an IDS under 37 CFR 1.97(c) where no statement under 1.97(e) was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 12.81 when reopening. To avoid abandonment appellant must either (1) file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111/1.113 or (2) request reinstatement of the appeal accompanied by a supplemental appeal brief (no new amendments/affidavits/evidence permitted). Supplemental brief may incorporate prior portions by reference and need only address issues relevant to the new ground(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief timing and examiner obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.193(b)(1) appellant may file a reply brief as a matter of right within 2 months from the mailing date of the examiner’s answer or supplemental examiner’s answer. The primary examiner must either acknowledge receipt and entry of the reply brief or withdraw the final rejection and reopen prosecution to respond to the reply brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions may be available under 37 CFR 1.136(b) or 1.550(c). A supplemental examiner’s answer is not permitted unless remanded by the Board. Amendments/affidavits/evidence must be submitted separately from the reply brief; documents that contain an amendment are not entitled to entry as a reply brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of reply brief (form and entry rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 12.47 may be used to acknowledge receipt and entry of a reply brief: 'The reply brief filed [3] has been entered and considered. The application has been forwarded to the Board ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment, affidavit, or declaration has been filed with the reply brief, the examiner must notify applicant whether it has been entered. Such materials should not be entered unless they place the application in condition for allowance (see 37 CFR 1.116 and 1.195).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request, fees, and basic limits
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.194: An oral hearing should be requested only when appellant considers such a hearing necessary or desirable. If appellant desires an oral hearing, appellant must file, in a separate paper, a written request for such hearing accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.17(d) within two months from the date of the examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no request/fee timely filed, appeal assigned for consideration/decision. If hearing set, oral argument normally limited to 20 minutes for appellant and 15 minutes for primary examiner unless otherwise ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing logistics and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of hearing (date/time/docket) is forwarded; if appellant fails to confirm, appeal removed from hearing docket and assigned on brief; no refund of fee. If confirmed but no appearance, appeal decided on brief. Telephone argument may be requested (appellant bears cost). Rescheduling discouraged and rarely granted without convincing reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant may request additional time in advance; final decision on extra time is by senior panel member. Examiner participation: if examiner wishes to present argument, include form paragraph 12.63 in Examiner’s Answer; examiner may attend as observer and should make notation on file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner participation at hearing (limits and notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant requested an oral hearing and the primary examiner wishes to appear and present an oral argument before the Board, a request to present oral argument must be included as last paragraph of the examiner’s answer (form paragraph 12.63). If the appellant’s request for hearing is filed after the examiner’s answer, the examiner’s request must be in an acknowledgement of reply brief or separate PTOL‑90 letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When examiner will present argument, the application file will be delivered to examiner at least 2 weeks prior; the Board may indicate specific points to address. After appellant's presentation examiner allowed 15 minutes to reply; appellant may use unused time for rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board jurisdiction transfer timing and effect on filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The application file and jurisdiction are normally transferred from Technology Centers to the Board: (A) After 2 months from the examiner’s answer, plus mail time, if no reply brief has been timely filed; (B) After a supplemental examiner’s answer pursuant to a remand; (C) After the examiner has notified appellant that the reply brief has been entered and considered and that the application will be forwarded to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment, affidavit, or other paper filed after transfer but before Board decision may be considered by the examiner only if the case is remanded by the Board for that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divided jurisdiction in interference-provoked appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appeal is taken from the second or final rejection only of one or more claims presented for the purpose of provoking an interference, jurisdiction of the rest of the case remains with the examiner, and prosecution of the remaining claims may proceed as though the entire case was under the examiner's jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the examiner certifies no conflict of subject matter and approval obtained, an appeal may proceed concurrently with an interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order for compliance (real party in interest / related cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may require the appellant to explicitly name the real party in interest or identify any related case; when the Board requires an explicit statement an order for compliance will set a 1‑month period for reply (37 CFR 1.192(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A simple paper identifying the real party in interest or stating none will suffice; extensions only under 37 CFR 1.136(b). Failure to timely respond may result in dismissal of the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand by Board (grounds and purposes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board has authority to remand a case to the examiner when necessary, e.g., for a fuller description of the claimed invention, to call upon the examiner for further explanation of references, to select a preferred ground among cumulative rejections, to remand for further search, or to consider an amendment/affidavit/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 12.80 may be used for a supplemental Examiner’s Answer on remand. Supervisory patent examiner should approve and Board notified whenever a remanded application is withdrawn from appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand to consider amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed amendment, affidavit, declaration, or other paper may be remanded for consideration; such an amendment will be treated as an amendment filed after appeal. The Board is not obligated to consider new or amended claims while it has jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposed amendment effectively abandons the appeal (e.g., cancels appealed claims), the amendment should be entered and clerk notified so the case may be removed from the Board’s docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand to consider affidavits or declarations (37 CFR 1.195)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits, declarations, or exhibits submitted after the case has been appealed will not be admitted without a showing of good and sufficient reasons why they were not earlier presented. Affidavits/declarations filed after the application has been forwarded to the Board but before decision cannot be considered by the examiner absent a remand; if remanded, examiner will consider merits if the required showing is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the affidavit/declaration lacks the required showing, the examiner will not consider it. The Board customarily will not remand affidavits/declarations offered in connection with a request for rehearing where no 1.196(b) rejection has been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand for further search
rubrics_metrics.description: Remand to the examiner for further search should be rare. A remand extends pendency and may necessitate an extension of patent term under 35 U.S.C. 154(b). When necessary, the Board should conduct a search of at least one subclass and cite art from that subclass to demonstrate the basis on which it concludes a search would be productive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The art cited need not be art upon which a rejection can be made; remand is disfavored because it prolongs prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may require appellant to address matters for decision (37 CFR 1.196(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may require appellant to address any matter deemed appropriate for a reasoned decision on the pending appeal and will give a non-extendable time period within which to respond; failure to respond within the time period will result in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include applicability of particular case law not previously identified or applicability of prior art not previously made of record. Making such a requirement is discretionary, and after appellant replies a remand may be appropriate.
